_v1_notes.FIRE BEHAVIOUR|SUPPRESSION ASSET: crown fire is N for hand crews and bulldozers - flame heights are beyond both, and putting people or machines in front of it is the classic fatality scenario. Spotting is N for hand crews, dozers and helicopters: new ignitions appear beyond any line these can hold, only broad retardant ahead of the front addresses it. Ground fire is N for fixed-wing retardant: a creeping smouldering fire is not what a large aerial load is for.
_v1_notes.FIRE BEHAVIOUR|WIND CONDITION: crown fire and spotting are both N in calm conditions - both require wind to occur at all.
_v1_notes.SUPPRESSION ASSET|TERRAIN: bulldozers are N on steep inaccessible slopes by definition, and N in the wildland urban interface where heavy machinery among structures is not used. Fixed-wing retardant is N in the interface: large chemical loads are not dropped over housing.
_v1_notes.SUPPRESSION ASSET|WIND CONDITION: helicopter drops are N in erratic gusting, and fixed-wing is N in both sustained strong wind and gusting - a long straight low approach is not survivable in either.
_v1_notes.TERRAIN|WIND CONDITION: no terrain excludes any wind condition.
